Rosa, the quarterly announcement was sent to all four countries this morning. Have you read it?
Twice. And there is one sentence I do not understand, or rather one sentence that does not want to be understood.
Which one?
"The corporate fare structure has been revised." That is the whole sentence. Who revised it, and when did that happen?
Pricing, in March, and the regional director signed off on it two weeks ago. It is not a secret. It is just written the way those emails are always written.

Good morning. This is the quarterly commercial announcement, and it is being sent to all commercial teams in the four countries. Three items. First, the regional office in Bogota has been fully staffed as of last week, and the remaining two positions were filled internally. Second, the new booking platform will be rolled out in March, and training sessions are going to be scheduled for every account manager before that date. Attendance is required. Third, the corporate fare structure has been revised. Existing contracts are not affected, and clients will be informed by their account manager, not by a central email. That last point is important. Nobody should hear this from a system.

Something I have learned about corporate writing, and I wish somebody had told me twenty years earlier. When you read a company announcement, ask one question of every sentence: who did this? Half the time the answer is right there. The other half, the sentence has been built so that the answer is missing. Mistakes were made. The decision was taken. The position has been eliminated. Nobody is lying, and often there is a good reason to leave the person out. But if you are the one writing, be careful. The passive is a wonderful tool for describing a process and a terrible way to deliver bad news, because the person receiving it always hears the same thing: somebody did this to me, and you will not say who.

Felipe says the quarterly announcement has been sent to all four countries and asks whether Rosa has read it. Rosa answers that she has read it twice and that one sentence is not clear. Felipe asks which sentence, and Rosa quotes the line about the fare structure being revised. Felipe explains who actually took the decision and why the announcement does not say so. Rosa says she will call her clients herself instead of letting them read it in a central email.
